target_customer: Institutional investors, asset managers and broker-dealers who trade through its auction venues and pay trading fees
problem: Continuous limit order book markets and dark pools handle large institutional orders poorly; OneChronos matches orders with combinatorial auctions that weigh complex trading preferences.
business_model: Transaction fees on matched trades via regulated alternative trading systems
product_category: Capital markets infrastructure (alternative trading system with combinatorial auctions)

founders.name: Kelly Littlepage
founders.background_notes: Gurobi case study says he studied combinatorial auction paradigms in academia; school and employers not found in sources opened.

founders.name: Stephen Johnson
founders.background_notes: Listed with Littlepage on the YC page; no background found.

competitors.name: IEX
competitors.what: Investor-owned venue with a speed bump aimed at protecting institutional orders; moved from ATS to exchange in 2016
competitors.traction_then: About 1.3 to 1.8 percent US equity share in Sept to Oct 2016
competitors.funding_then: Owned by buy-side firms; not stated

technical_complexity.rationale: Combinatorial optimization matching run many times per second, plus regulated broker-dealer and ATS build-out; hard for a small team in 2016.

defensibility.rationale: ATS and broker-dealer registration, exchange connectivity and liquidity from institutions are slow to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Cboe added a periodic auction order type in April 2022, a related but different mechanism; no acquisition found.

market_need_then: 2016 saw debate over high-frequency trading and the approval of IEX as an exchange, showing buy-side demand for fairer venues.

branding.domain_note: Uses onechronos.com; no acquisition story found.

identity.logo: Wordmark; not described by sources opened
identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and institutional, centered on smart markets and auctions

branding.community_and_virality: No community or merch found; coverage is trade press.

brand_strength.rationale: Niche institutional brand known mainly in trading circles; no brand-level press found. Chronos is the Greek word for time but no source explains the choice.

pivots.to: Adding auction markets for GPU compute and other asset classes
pivots.why: Extension announced with Auctionomics (company site and Substack coverage)

outcome_analysis: OneChronos spent several years on regulatory build-out, filed its Form ATS-N in 2020 and launched its equities ATS around 2021 and 2022, then raised a 40 million dollar Series B in 2023 and a 32 million dollar round in 2024. It added UK approval and a compute auction market, and remains active with about 75 staff.
notes: BusinessWire releases for the 2023 and 2024 rounds returned 403 and were not worked around; the 2023 Series B 40 million and Addition lead come from search snippets of Serrari and startupintros (aggregator-like), and 2024 32 million is confirmed by The Trade News (investors not named there, Addition from search summaries). Aggregators total 72 to 81 million, so earlier seed and Series A rounds likely exist but were not found. The IEX competitor source is dated Oct 2016, a few months after the batch. Outcome search found no acquisition, layoffs or controversy.
